title: Async request fanout strategy scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for an asynchronous request fanout strategy for client-side and edge proxies. Goal: improve tail latency and P99 across mixed workloads by spec-ing a safe way to simultaneously query multiple model variants or routes and merge partial/first-good responses while bounding cost and telemetry complexity.

Background/constraints:
- We serve similar prompts to several compatible model types (e.g., small low-cost, medium quantized, large high-quality).
- Many customers prefer single-call semantics and predictable billing.
- Any fanout must not explode token costs or leak sensitive context to unintended backends.
- We need clear traces for debugging and SLO attribution.

High level idea:
1) Candidate selection: client proxy picks 1-3 target routes based on policy (latency SLO, budget, historic quality).
2) Staged fanout: send to primary immediately; schedule secondary(s) with small delays (staggered) or conditional triggers (primary slow or low-confidence partial).
3) Merge/short-circuit: return as soon as a response meets acceptance criteria (latency threshold + quality proxy). Cancel in-flight slower requests to save cost where possible.
4) Record lineage: attribution id on each call; ensure canceled RPCs still emit minimal telemetry and cost tags.

API shape sketch (client proxy <-> runtime router):
- POST /v1/fanout/generate
  body: { prompt: string, fanout_policy: string, budget_token_limit: int, accept_rules: ["first_non_empty", "score_threshold:0.7"], trace_id: string }
- Response: { result: string, chosen_route: string, route_scores: [ {route, latency_ms, confidence_est} ], partials: [ route -> truncated content if returned earlier ] }

Example fanout_policy presets:
- single-fast: primary only, no fanout
- hedge-1: primary + one hedged replica after 50ms if no response
- quality-first: primary=high-quality, fallback cheap after 200ms; never cancel primary until full token budget used

Acceptance/quality heuristics (lightweight):
- token-count heuristic: if response < N tokens after T ms, consider low-confidence and trigger a backup
- language-model score proxy: use simple scoring function from logprobs if available (> threshold)
- prefix match: partial is acceptable if last token is whitespace/newline (avoid mid-token cutoffs)

Cost controls:
- budget_token_limit on request enforced at router; proxies decrement a soft budget counter per tenant for fanout allowances
- per-tenant fanout_rate_limit: X fanouts per minute; fallback to single route when exceeded

Telemetry/tracing:
- every request has fanout_trace_id; each subcall annotated with path and decision reason (staggered, slow_primary, low_confidence)
- emit event when a cancelled call had already consumed >Y tokens (for billing/alerts)
- sample full transcripts only for failure/debug traces, otherwise send aggregated metrics

Edge cases and privacy:
- secret-scoped models: disallow fanout to models that are not authorized for a tenant (enforce ACL check at candidate selection)
- PII minimization: redact attributes in telemetry; do not forward full user payload to any model not in tenant's allowlist

ASCII flow sketch:
Client -> Proxy [select candidates] -> Primary -> Router -> ModelA
                             |-> delayed start -> ModelB
                             |-> conditional start -> ModelC
Return earliest acceptable result to Client; send cancellation signal to remaining inflight.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define a small, fast confidence proxy that doesn't require full scoring from model (cheap heuristic vs full eval).
- How to expose per-request fanout budget in public API without confusing billing? (suggest: non-default, enterprise opt-in)
- Cancellation semantics: best-effort vs guaranteed stop; how to surface partial token costs to clients?
- Implementation plan: prototype in client-proxy, add metrics and a canary in a low-traffic onboarded tenant, evaluate cost delta and P99 improvement.

Notes on prototype telemetry schema (very compact):
- fanout_trace_id, request_id, chosen_route, decision_reason, latency_chosen_ms, tokens_chosen, cancelled_routes=[route:tokens_consumed], budget_limit

Quick experiment plan:
- Canary 1: hedge-1 policy on 5% traffic for latency-sensitive route; measure P50/P95/P99 and cost delta after 2 weeks
- Canary 2: quality-first on 1% traffic for a high-value tenant to validate quality improvements

Links and references:
- ENG-1723 (proposal ticket)
- runtime PR linked above (prototype skeleton)

Final: rough and messy. This doc is personal workspace; refine into an eng RFC if canary results look promising.
